target_customer: Urban and tourist riders in Indian cities renting two-wheelers by the hour, day or month, plus local rental shop partners
problem: Renting a bike in India was fragmented across small shops with no easy online booking or transparent pricing.
business_model: Marketplace aggregator taking a commission from rental vendors, later adding its own dockless scooter service (Go)

founders.name: Pranay Shrivastava
previous_startups: Pankhuri (social commerce, founded 2019 per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists his WheelStreet role as 2016 to 2019.

founders.name: Moksha Srivastava
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CMO on the YC page and in TechCrunch (2017-12-18).

founders.name: Mrityunjay Jha
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2017-12-18) says Moksha started the company with friends Mrityunjay Jha and Pranay Shrivastava. Other outlets spell the name differently.

competitors.name: Zoomcar
competitors.what: Self-drive car rental marketplace named as a rental rival
competitors.traction_then: named in December 2017 coverage of WheelStreet Go

competitors.name: Ola and Uber
competitors.what: Ride-hailing, said to account for 60 percent of tier-one city transportation
competitors.traction_then: dominant in tier-one cities per the article

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking marketplace over partner shop inventory; the dockless scooter service added IoT and logistics but was a pilot of 50 scooters.

defensibility.rationale: Supply of vendors across 33 cities gave some marketplace effects, but vendors could list elsewhere and the model was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ola-backed Vogo and Bounce (both funded after the batch) moved into dockless scooter rental in 2018 and 2019 per later coverage; WheelStreet's own fate is not documented.

market_need_then: India had a large two-wheeler base and tourist rental demand; the company said its marketplace was nearly at breakeven in late 2017 and planned to raise about $2M to scale Go.

branding.domain_note: Used wheelstreet.com, which now serves a blank page

identity.voice_and_tone: Offers free helmets, unlimited kilometres and home delivery per the YC page

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in YourStory, Inc42, Entrepreneur India and TechCrunch; no evidence of fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Reasonable regional press and a clear descriptive name, but no signature asset and no brand material found.

pivots.from: Aggregator marketplace for rental shop bikes
pivots.to: Adding Go, a dockless scooter service in Bangalore
pivots.why: To compete with dockless sharing models such as Mobike and Ofo; the company planned 25,000 scooters by end of 2018

outcome_analysis: WheelStreet launched in 2014 as a bike rental aggregator, raised about $500K in March 2016 and Y Combinator money in 2017, and reported near breakeven on its marketplace while piloting 50 Go scooters in December 2017. YC now lists it inactive and its founder's YC bio dates his WheelStreet role as 2016 to 2019. No article or company notice explains a shutdown or its cause, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Stage labels: sources call Broadbean a seed and pre-Series A fund and one summary says pre-seed, so the stage is recorded as other. The Broadbean round is stated by Business Standard, Inc42 and DealStreetAsia (seen as search results). The Y Combinator $120K round is dated September 2017 by a syndicated article and August 2017 by Inc42, recorded as 2017; CB Insights dates it July 2020, which conflicts, and Seedtable shows no rounds. Totals of $620K to $640K are reported by CB Insights, Inc42 and Indian Startup Times. Exit unknown: YC status Inactive but no shutdown source. The 2017 article says WheelStreet was raising about $2M, with no evidence it closed. Founders' prior employers and education not found in opened sources.
